name: Carrion Defense Works Marrow Drill MD-7 'Dentist'
description: A heavy-frame pistol firing gyroscopically stabilized micro-bore rounds that rotate at 14,000 RPM upon leaving the barrel. The rounds are designed to defeat rigid armor by drilling through rather than punching through, maintaining a tight wound channel that resists emergency sealing. Carrion's marketing materials describe it as 'persistent access' ammunition. Medical personnel call it something else entirely.
legality: Restricted — military and licensed contractors only
specifications:
caliber: 4.5mm gyrostabilized micro-bore
magazine: 8 rounds
muzzle velocity: 410 m/s with 14,000 RPM spin
effective range: 5-20 meters
weight: 1.4 kg
barrel life: approximately 200 rounds before rifling degradation
story_hooks: Forensic teams have identified MD-7 wound channels in three separate unsolved killings across different tiers — the same weapon, same operator, different political targets.
A Carrion engineer has gone missing after posting internal documents showing the MD-7 was originally designed for surgical applications before being reclassified as ordnance.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist slab of engineering—squat, aggressive, purposefully ugly. The Marrow Drill presents as a compact but dense pistol with an oversized, ribbed barrel assembly that dominates the weapon's profile. The receiver sits stubby and utilitarian beneath, with no ergonomic flourishes. It reads as medical apparatus as much as firearm: clinical, precise, designed to penetrate rather than impress.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 18 cm | Width: 4.2 cm | Height: 12 cm | Barrel length: 8.5 cm with rifling shroud
physical_description.weight_description: Dense and front-heavy. The 1.4 kg mass concentrates forward in the barrel assembly, creating a pronounced muzzle-down feel that demands two-handed grip. It sits in the palm like a sculptor's hammer.
physical_description.primary_material: Hardened steel frame with tungsten-carbide lined micro-bore barrel. Polymer grip module (reinforced nylon composite, Tier 3 standard). Rifling shroud in brushed titanium.
physical_description.finish: Matte black industrial coating with aggressive micro-texturing. The barrel shroud exhibits worn, burnished titanium showing tool marks and stress patterns. Frame shows service scratches and faint oxidation at stress points.
physical_description.color_scheme: Soot black primary with brushed titanium accents on the barrel assembly. No bright trim—all functional surfaces are intentionally desaturated.
physical_description.grip_texture: Coarse, deeply cross-hatched polymer with embedded grip rail channels. Designed for gloved hands—unforgiving, non-slip, cold to bare skin. Slight chemical smell of hardened composite.
distinctive_features: Oversized ribbed barrel shroud with visible cooling fins running the length of the muzzle
Recessed rifling inspection port on the barrel—shows internal spiral grooves
Minimal sights: simple post and notch, painted dull grey, clearly secondary to ballistics computer integration
Aggressive front serrations running from frame to muzzle shroud
Magazine well is deep-cut, almost a recess; uses proprietary 8-round caseless magazines with visible ammunition spinning mechanism
Ambidextrous safety selector positioned high and prominent—military contractor spec
Two-line engraving on the slide: 'CARRION DEFENSE WORKS' and 'MD-7 PERSISTENT ACCESS'
Wear patterns: carbon scoring around muzzle exit, micro-fractures in polymer grip from repeated holstering, barrel shroud shows heat discoloration rings
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Carrion Defense Works logo (angular, predatory bird silhouette) stamped into the frame above the trigger guard. Model designation 'MD-7' laser-etched into the barrel shroud. Serial number on frame interior. Military contractor provisioning codes micro-stamped on the magazine well.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but visibly used. Barrel shows light fouling visible through the inspection port. Polymer grip exhibits character—small cracks, smoothing from repeated draws, possible tape repair at frame juncture. Owner-maintained, professional condition; never mall-queen, always field-ready.
